chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no problem if you sell to the man the goods that are not with you, haggling over them, then you buy for him approximately that which he sought, then make it binding upon yourself, then you sell it to him afterwards.

key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: goods, merchandise, or items for sale
key_terms.تُوجِبُهُ: making it binding or obligatory upon oneself

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods you do not yet possess in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi validates the permissibility of selling what is not in one's possession (bay' al-ma'mul bihi) by structuring it as a two-step process: selling the item to a buyer, then purchasing the specific goods to fulfill that obligation, and finally delivering them. It highlights the flexibility in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding deferred delivery, provided the seller binds the acquisition to the initial sale, distinguishing it from the stricter prohibitions on pure uncertainty (gharar).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin suweyd, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is no problem if you were to sell to the man the goods which are not with you, fixing the price of it. Then you buy for him approximately that which he seeks, then make it binding upon yourself, then you sell it to him afterwards’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It is lawful for a man to sell goods which are not with him in the form of Musawamah (fixed price regardless of capital), then buy for him the goods he demands and make it necessary for yourself thereafter to ask him to sell it to you.’”
